summary: Port Pontchartrain light at Milneburg, New Orleans: an 1855 brick tower kept by women from 1882; discontinued in 1928 or 1929.

lens.note: Original fifth-order Fresnel, installed 1857 (archive); current optic none (archive).

structures.note: 28 ft tall; built after the 1834 appropriation (LighthouseFriends). Replaced by the brick tower.
Built on a concrete pad on pilings about 2,100 ft offshore; 36 ft base to lantern center; 47 ft above mean high water (archive); top widened and raised about 7 ft in 1880 (LighthouseFriends).

access.note: Not open to the public (archive). Grounds open, tower closed (LighthouseFriends).

facts.agency: University of New Orleans (owner, per LighthouseFriends)

events.note: Year established per the archive. LighthouseFriends describes a railroad company light first, then a government tower after 1834.
Benjamin J. Shane becomes first keeper, 15 Feb 1839.
Congress appropriates $6,000 to replace the old tower at the port (3 Aug 1854, per LighthouseFriends).
Brick tower completed on piles offshore.
Original fifth-order Fresnel lens (archive). LighthouseFriends says the lens was installed at completion in 1855.
Top widened and tower raised about seven feet for a new lantern room.
Ellen Wilson, first of three women principal keepers.
Keeper at Head of Passes drowns (per LighthouseFriends). Margaret R. Norvell enters service in April 1891 as assistant keeper at Head of Passes, after her husband's death (Bulletin 1932).
Repairs to revolving machinery; light to be changed to fixed white (Light-House Board report for the fiscal year ended 30 June 1900, item 1043).
Storm of 1903 (quoted by LighthouseFriends from the Morning Tribune, 26 June 1932): station the only building left standing on the lower coast.
On 16 September Norvell cares for a man taken ill aboard the steamer Hanover until his death; commended.
Hurricane at New Orleans, 29 September 1915; Port Pontchartrain light station damaged.
Norvell moves to New Canal light; Minnie E. Coteron takes charge at Port Pontchartrain.
Discontinued 1929 (archive place record; Rowlett's directory per the record).
University of New Orleans acquires the land from the Orleans Levee District (LighthouseFriends); the lighthouse is now on the university's Research and Technology Park grounds.

keepers.note: Bulletins 1914 and 1932 print Maggie R. Norvell; the 1912-17 index prints Maggie H.; LighthouseFriends prints Margaret. corrections.why: The place is spelled Milneburg in the archive's alternate name and in LighthouseFriends; the story uses Milneburg. The record's spelling may be a variant the editor prefers to keep.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: LighthouseFriends says she was appointed in her husband's place; the 1932 bulletin says she entered the service in April 1891 as an assistant keeper at Head of Passes after his death. The story gives both.
The archive lists the station as not open to the public; LighthouseFriends says the grounds are open and the tower closed. The story gives both.

LighthouseFriends gives the discontinuance as 10 May 1928, which matches the last keeper's stint ending in 1928 on the roster. The archive's 'Year Discontinued' and the record's Rowlett-sourced date give 1929. The story gives both.

LighthouseFriends says the fifth-order Fresnel was equipped when the tower was completed in 1855. The archive gives 1857 as the year the original lens was installed. The story gives the archive's date and notes the difference.

The archive's 'Year Established' is 1832. LighthouseFriends says a railroad company's light stood first, then Congress allocated money in 1834 and a wooden tower followed. It is not clear which light the 1832 date refers to. The story does not give 1832 as a date for a government light.

The 1914 and 1932 bulletins print Maggie R. Norvell, the 1912-17 index prints Maggie H., and the roster and LighthouseFriends print Margaret R. Norvell. The story uses Margaret, matching the roster, and notes the bulletins' name.

notes_for_editor: Roster matched by name (port-pontchartrain); the archive's position is 4.6 km from the station and rounded to the minute, so the match was checked against the place name. Roster lines and person slugs come from roster.py --json. LighthouseFriends is secondary and copyrighted: the story paraphrases it and uses at most short phrases; the 1903 storm account is the Morning Tribune of 26 June 1932 as quoted by LighthouseFriends; the newspaper itself was not found in Chronicling America (two Louisiana searches returned nothing usable). The 1915 Bulletin page 41 text is OCR-damaged ('cbaracter', 'Pontchartl'ain'); quotes copied as read. The 1932 retirement month (April 30) is OCR-garbled ('SO') in the bulletin; the story says April 1932 from that reading. The Light-House Board volumes after 1901 are not in the corpus, so the Board's 1904-1928 reports were not checked; the 1900 entry is item 1043 at scan page 153 of the volume labelled 1900. The Rowlett-sourced 1832 first-light date is not confirmed by any government source read. The 1869 hurricane and the family tradition about Shane come from LighthouseFriends only. Pontchartrain Beach and UNO facts are LighthouseFriends only. Confidence medium: keepers and the Bulletin events are primary; the early history is LighthouseFriends.
